meta.title: The Dam the River Took Back
meta.skill_frame: Text structure: follow a cause whose effect arrives years later.

reader.who: Older students who read at about a fourth-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: Measured FK 6.4, 5.7 and 6.8 on the three parts (104, 104 and 103 words), 6.3 together, near the band's ceiling. The load is a delay: one action, a first effect that looks like failure, a second effect that only arrives after the river has moved the silt, and a third that depends on the second. The reader must keep the order of the effects apart.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.attribution: Original text drafted for text_structure 4.1, Band 4.1, sequence 2. No external work.
source.text_status: Drafted for the band, accepted on spot check.
source.survey: A river restoration told as a delayed chain: the first year looks like damage and the fourth looks like success, which is the structure the items test.
source.avoided: No river, state, agency, or dam date. No fish species named. No cost or acreage figures.

session.difficulty_basis: Items 1-3 take stated facts; 4-5 join a slow process to its delayed result.

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: A mill dam held back a river for ninety years. Behind the dam the water slowed, and everything the river carried settled to the bottom of the pond. Silt, sand, and old leaves built up in a layer several feet deep, and the pond grew shallow and warm in the summer sun. Fish that needed clean gravel to spawn could not swim past the dam at all. When the dam finally came out, the river did not return to its old shape in one season. The first year brought a rush of trapped silt downstream, and it coated the gravel beds the fish needed.
passage.part_2: The harm looked worse than the dam had, and the neighbors said so. They saw brown water and bare banks and concluded that the removal had failed. But the river was doing its slow work. Each spring flood lifted some of the loose silt from the bottom and carried it farther downstream. Gravel that had been buried for decades came back into the current, where moving water washed it clean. By the third year the stones below the old dam were scoured and bright again, and the water ran clear past the banks that had been brown. The banks themselves settled within a season.
passage.part_3: Fish arrived after the gravel, not before it. Young fish swam up from the larger river in the fourth spring, when the clean stones were finally ready. Biologists who counted the young fish had expected them a year sooner. Their first report called the project slow. The river was not behind schedule, because a river keeps no schedule at all. A dam can be removed in an afternoon, but a river needs years to repair what stood behind it. That gap between the work and the result is why the first summer looked like a mistake and the fifth looked like a success.

items.prompt: Why could the fish not spawn while the dam stood?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. The dam stopped them from reaching the clean gravel.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The part says fish needed clean gravel to spawn and could not swim past the dam at all.
tutor_only.tell: The gravel was upstream and the dam was in the way. The fish could not reach the beds they needed.
help: Find the sentence about what the fish needed.
It names the gravel, and the dam stood between the fish and it.
tutor_only.core_idea: The dam blocked the fish from the gravel they needed.
accept_ideas: the dam blocked them from the gravel
they could not swim past the dam
the gravel was above the dam
not_required: how many fish lived below the dam
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the water was too warm
if_they_say.ask: Warmth is mentioned about the pond, not as the reason the fish could not spawn. What stood in their way?

items.prompt: What happened to the gravel in the first year after the dam came out?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. A rush of silt came downstream and coated it.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The last sentence says the first year brought a rush of trapped silt downstream, and it coated the gravel beds.
tutor_only.tell: Taking out the dam released the silt it had been holding. The first effect was mud on the stones the fish needed.
help: Read the last sentence of this part.
It says what the silt did to the gravel beds.
tutor_only.core_idea: Silt came downstream and coated the gravel.
accept_ideas: silt washed down and covered the gravel
the gravel was buried in silt
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the gravel washed away
if_they_say.ask: The gravel was covered, not carried off. What settled on top of it?

items.prompt: Why did the neighbors think the removal had failed?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. They saw brown water and bare banks and drew a conclusion from what they could see.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The part says they saw brown water and bare banks and concluded that the removal had failed.
tutor_only.tell: They judged by the first summer. Brown water and bare banks looked like damage, and the slow work underneath was invisible.
help: Find the sentence that begins 'They saw brown water'.
It names what they saw and what they decided.
tutor_only.core_idea: They saw brown water and bare banks and thought the removal had failed.
accept_ideas: it looked worse than before the dam came out
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the river flooded
if_they_say.ask: Flooding is not mentioned. What did the neighbors see in the water and on the banks?

items.prompt: Why were the stones clean only in the third year?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. The river had to carry the silt away first, and each spring flood moved some of it.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The part says each spring flood lifted some of the loose silt and carried it farther, and by the third year the stones were scoured and bright.
tutor_only.tell: The stones could not be cleaned while the silt lay on them. The river moved the silt a little each spring, and only then could the current reach the gravel.
help: Read the sentence about the spring floods.
It says what the floods did to the silt, and what that let happen to the stones.
tutor_only.core_idea: The floods had to move the silt before the current could scour the stones.
accept_ideas: the floods had to wash the silt away first
the silt had to move downstream
each spring carried more silt away
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says new gravel arrived
if_they_say.ask: The part says gravel that had been buried came back into the current. What did the floods move off it?

items.prompt: The passage says a dam comes out in an afternoon but a river needs years. What does that mean here?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. Taking the dam out was quick, but the river's repair took years.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage contrasts an afternoon's work with years of silt moving, gravel scouring, and fish returning in the fourth spring.
tutor_only.tell: The two clocks are different. A crew can take a dam down in a day. The river then needs years to move the silt and clean the stones.
help: Compare the last part's sentence about an afternoon with the years the river took.
One is the work of people, and the other is the work of water.
tutor_only.core_idea: Removing the dam was quick, but the river's recovery took years.
accept_ideas: the work was fast but the river's fix was slow
the river needed years to clean itself
taking the dam out was easy next to the river repairing the damage
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the river was slow to freeze
if_they_say.ask: The passage is about silt and gravel, not freezing. Which part of the work took years?
